title: DataAccessV1dot19
description: K-05 v1.19, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1455: the reads journey 1's first calls need that v1.18 lacks, from T-632's handoff, on the sign-up chain; DL-867, DL-949). It only adds to v1.18 (data-access.v1.18.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.18 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none is restated, so every v1 to v1.18 exchange is a v1.19 exchange. Added: two reads on the primary, uncached, each in one read-only transaction, each row answered with its id (or, for a row whose primary key is two columns, the name README item 77 gives it) and its version (limit 4): readKindCatalog (README item 78: the kind matcher's catalog, every K-24 kinds row whose source is trade_file, shared reference data with no business column, read by the Tool API's client, rosie_app, under any business scope or none; never a drafted kind) and readPickedKinds (README item 79: the owner's kinds of work as sign-up holds them, K-24 picked_kinds with each pick's picked_kind_texts by key and version, its new_work_drafts row and that draft's new_work_draft_blocks, and K-23 companies: the call's business's rows and the call's person's rows with no business, read on the runtime side as rosie_job with that rule in every statement). Every column answered is named; never a person's address or number, a plug-in block's text or a draft block's answer. No call, write, state, column, grant, index or migration is added beyond these reads. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

kindPattern.title: KindPattern
kindPattern.description: A kind of work's booking pattern, one of the 11 of FS section 3 (K-24 v1 kinds_pattern_known; SPEC-prof 2 item 5): what the customer picks and how the time is held, as the matcher reads it beside the name and style (README item 78). New in v1.19.

kindCatalogRow.title: KindCatalogRow
kindCatalogRow.description: One kind of the matcher's catalog, a K-24 v1 kinds row whose source is trade_file, as readKindCatalog answers it (README item 78), shaped to T-632's CatalogKind (actions/src/domain/kind-matcher/matcher.ts): its id, name, style, pattern and source, with the row's version beside them (limit 4). Never its facts, the trade's default facts S1-04 reads by id through readTurnState (refuse-kind-catalog-with-facts), and never a drafted kind (refuse-kind-catalog-drafted-kind). New in v1.19.

id.description: kinds.id, the trade file's id, such as barber or plumber (K-01 v1 tradeId): the row's one-column primary key, so its id in a K-05 row reference (table kinds).

name.description: kinds.name, the trade file's name, such as Barber: the words the matcher weighs most, and the name K-09 matchKinds offers (KindFound.name).

style.description: kinds.style, the booking type in words, such as Chair or Home visit: never null for a trade-file kind (kinds_trade_file_has_style).

pattern.description: kinds.pattern, such as chair or fix.

source.description: kinds.source: trade_file, the one source the catalog answers (K-24 README line 96: the matcher offers only trade_file kinds; a drafted kind stays with its owner).

readKindCatalog.request.title: ReadKindCatalogRequest
readKindCatalog.request.description: The kind matcher's catalog (T-632's CatalogKind list; S1-02; README item 78): every K-24 kinds row whose source is trade_file. The request names nothing: the catalog is shared reference data with no business column (K-24 README rule 2: scope none), so it answers the same rows under any business and under none, and a business named would read as a filter the read never applies (refuse-kind-catalog-names-business). Scope and role: the Tool API's client, rosie_app, in the call's own transaction under whatever business scope it holds, which does not narrow the catalog (no row-level security on kinds, and rosie_app holds SELECT on it: 0021); rosie_job holds the same SELECT, so a runtime-side caller reads it the same way. Reads: the primary, uncached, one read-only transaction. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources (K-09 matchKinds proposes at most 200 ms: its README default 3). New in v1.19.

readKindCatalog.response.title: ReadKindCatalogResponse
readKindCatalog.response.description: kinds, every trade-file kinds row in id order, compared byte by byte (the matcher's own order: matcher.ts offered()), never a drafted kind; empty only when the catalog seed has not run (K-24 README rule 7), which the matcher refuses (T-632 default 4: KindCatalogError), so S1-02 asks again later and nothing is picked (README item 78, default 170). New in v1.19.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readKindCatalog.errors.title: ReadKindCatalogErrors
readKindCatalog.errors.description: transient alone: the catalog names no business and no row, so nothing can be not found. The binding fails closed on it: a thrown error, never an empty list (README item 78). New in v1.19.

pickOutcome.title: PickOutcome
pickOutcome.description: What a pick became (K-24 v1 picked_kinds_outcome_known; S1-02's three branches): listed, a kind on Rosie's list; new_work, not on the list yet, drafted for Rosie's team to review (S1-03); not_booked, not a service Rosie books, set up nowhere and kept so Rosie's team sees the owner's words (S1-74). New in v1.19.

pfKey.title: PluginTextKey
pfKey.description: One of the 11 free-text plug-in keys S1-11 gives (K-24 v1 picked_kind_texts_key_known; MC R3; Q-39), never a typed key (pf.facts, pf.switches and pf.settings are K-23's and K-24's typed columns). New in v1.19.

pickTextRowId.title: PickTextRowId
pickTextRowId.description: The name every K-05 row reference gives a K-24 v1 picked_kind_texts row, whose primary key is two columns (picked_kind_id, pf_key): <pick id>/<pf key>, such as pick-sam-barbershop/pf.rules (README item 77; db/repo/setup/row-names.ts). A pf key holds no slash (picked_kind_texts_key_known), so no two rows share a name; the database builds the name from the row's own columns and compares it whole, never split (CQ-09). The pf key alone names no row (refuse-picked-kinds-text-by-key-alone). New in v1.19.

draftBlockRowId.title: DraftBlockRowId
draftBlockRowId.description: The name every K-05 row reference gives a K-24 v1 new_work_draft_blocks row, whose primary key is two columns (draft_id, block): <draft id>/<block>, the block's number as text, such as draft-pack-hikes/4 (README item 77; db/repo/setup/row-names.ts). A block is 1 to 15 (new_work_draft_blocks_block_range), so no two rows share a name. Built and compared as pickTextRowId says. New in v1.19.

pickTextRead.title: PickTextRead
pickTextRead.description: One of a pick's plug-in text blocks, a K-24 v1 picked_kind_texts row, as readPickedKinds answers it (README item 79): which pf key is loaded, with the row's name, business and version, never the block's text, which a step that needs it reads by this name through readTurnState (S1-08's pf.rules; README default 175). New in v1.19.

businessId.description: picked_kind_texts.business_id: its pick's business, or null while the pick has none (picked_kind_texts_pick_business_fk).

draftBlockRead.title: DraftBlockRead
draftBlockRead.description: One answered block of a new-work draft's checklist, a K-24 v1 new_work_draft_blocks row, as readPickedKinds answers it (README item 79): the block, the owner's answer or clear no, and the facts and switches it set, with the row's name, business and version. Never the answer's words, the owner's own (refuse-picked-kinds-draft-block-answer; README default 176). A block with no row is still at its safe default (K-24 README 'Picks, text blocks and drafts'). New in v1.19.

block.description: new_work_draft_blocks.block, the block's number on S1-03's checklist.

businessId.description: new_work_draft_blocks.business_id: its draft's business, or null while the draft has none.

outcome.description: new_work_draft_blocks.outcome: answered, or no, the owner's clear no, which sets nothing.

factsOn.description: new_work_draft_blocks.facts_on, as stored: empty for a no.

switchesOn.description: new_work_draft_blocks.switches_on, as stored, in both flows: empty for a no.

newWorkDraftRead.title: NewWorkDraftRead
newWorkDraftRead.description: A new_work pick's draft, its K-24 v1 new_work_drafts row, as readPickedKinds answers it (README item 79): its id, business, state, when it was started and version, with every block answered so far, in block order. Offline until approved (S1-03); the team's decision writes its state (K-09 decideReviewItem). New in v1.19.

id.description: new_work_drafts.id, which K-37's review item names as its subject (subject_table new_work_drafts).

businessId.description: new_work_drafts.business_id: its pick's business, or null while the pick has none.

state.description: new_work_drafts.state: drafting, in_review (the team's review item is open), approved or kept_offline.

pickedKindRead.title: PickedKindRead
pickedKindRead.description: One kind of work an owner named, a K-24 v1 picked_kinds row, as readPickedKinds answers it (README item 79): every column, with the pf keys of its plug-in text blocks loaded so far (S1-11) and, for a new_work pick, its draft (S1-03). New in v1.19.

id.description: picked_kinds.id: the row's one-column primary key, its id in a K-05 row reference (table picked_kinds), and the pick K-09 SetupS1_03, SetupS1_11 and SetupS1_04 name.

ownerPersonId.description: picked_kinds.owner_person_id: who named it (K-04 persons.id), never their name or contact.

position.description: picked_kinds.position: its place in the order the owner named the kinds, from 1 (S1-02: the first named is set up first).

words.description: picked_kinds.words: the owner's own words for this kind, as S1-02 took them, such as Barbershop or plumbing (audience owner), which S1-04's answer is matched to and S1-08's plan names the kind by (README default 177).

kindId.description: picked_kinds.kind_id: a trade-file kind when listed, the drafted kind (new-...) when new_work, null when not_booked (picked_kinds_kind_unless_not_booked).

companyId.description: picked_kinds.company_id (K-23 companies.id), set at S1-04; null until then, and for work not booked.

businessId.description: picked_kinds.business_id: the business it is for, or null while there is none (a sign-up before S1-04 or S1-09 sets it).

texts.description: Its picked_kind_texts rows, in pf key order compared byte by byte: none until S1-11 loads the kind ('the barbershop's now, and plumbing's and electrical's when Sam gets to them').

draft.description: Its new_work_drafts row with its blocks, or null: only a new_work pick has one (new_work_drafts_one_per_pick; that the pick is new_work is code's, K-24).

companyRead.title: CompanyRead
companyRead.description: One of the owner's companies, a K-23 v1 companies row, as readPickedKinds answers it (README item 79): its id, owner, name, business and version, so S1-04 places a pick in a company already made rather than a second of the same name, and S1-08 names the companies in the plan. Its kinds are its picks' (companyId) and K-23 company_kinds, which v1.18's readBusinessKinds lists once the business exists. New in v1.19.

id.description: companies.id: the row's one-column primary key, its id in a K-05 row reference (table companies).

ownerPersonId.description: companies.owner_person_id (K-04 persons.id), never their name or contact.

name.description: companies.name, such as Lee Home Services LLC (FS row B10).

businessId.description: companies.business_id: its business, or null until S1-09 gives it one (K-23 README 'Companies and kinds').

pickedKindsNotFoundError.title: PickedKindsNotFoundError
pickedKindsNotFoundError.description: notFound with table persons (the request's person does not exist) or businesses (the request's business does not exist), so readPickedKinds never answers empty lists for a person or a business that is not there (README item 79, default 174). Nothing was read beyond them. New in v1.19.

readPickedKinds.request.title: ReadPickedKindsRequest
readPickedKinds.request.description: The owner's kinds of work as sign-up holds them (S1-02, S1-03, S1-74, S1-11, S1-04 and S1-08; README item 79): every K-24 picked_kinds row with its text blocks' keys, its draft and the draft's blocks, and every K-23 companies row, of the call's business, and of the call's person with no business. Both are stated: the business, or null for a sign-up before its business (refuse-picked-kinds-business-left-out), and the person, never null (refuse-picked-kinds-no-person). Scope and role: rosie_job, in one read-only transaction at repeatable read, so one snapshot: persons first; with a business, the transaction's scope set to it and confirmed by requireBusinessScope() before businesses and the business's rows are read, since a Tool API call never runs with no scope (db/repo scope.ts, T-1094; QUESTIONS.md CQ-70), then the scope cleared and confirmed empty before the person's rows with no business, which no business scope sees (K-23 README rule 5; K-24 README 'Picks, text blocks and drafts'); with businessId null, those alone, on the runtime side. Every statement carries the rule itself (business_id = the request's business, or business_id is null and owner_person_id = the request's person), and each text, draft and block is joined to its pick under it (README item 79, defaults 171 and 180). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources. New in v1.19.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (K-09 caller.businessId), whose rows are read, or null for a sign-up before its business.

personId.description: The call's own person (K-09 caller.personId: the turn party's person, or a page's signed-in person), whose rows with no business are read; never a person named in words.

readPickedKinds.response.title: ReadPickedKindsResponse
readPickedKinds.response.description: picks, every picked_kinds row of the request's business and every one of the request's person with no business, in (picked_at, position, id) order, the order the owner named them, each with its text blocks' keys, and its draft with its blocks or null; companies, every companies row of the business and every one of the person with no business, in id order; ids compared byte by byte. Never another business's row and never another person's row with no business; empty lists when there are none (README item 79). New in v1.19.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readPickedKinds.errors.title: ReadPickedKindsErrors
readPickedKinds.errors.description: notFound (table persons or businesses): the request's person or business does not exist; transient. The binding fails closed on either: a thrown error, never empty lists (README item 79). New in v1.19.
